---
title: "PIX Payments"
description: "Create PIX payments and generate QR codes"
---


Create PIX (Brazilian Instant Payment) transactions and generate QR codes that customers can scan to complete payments instantly.

## Endpoint

```http
POST /api/v1/transactions/payments/pix
```

## Overview

PIX is Brazil's instant payment system that allows real-time transfers 24/7. It's the most popular payment method in Brazil and supports payments in Brazilian Real (BRL).

## Request

<Request>
  <Title>CreatePixPaymentRequest</Title>
  ```json
  {
    "amount": 2050,
    "currency": "BRL",
    "expires_in": 1800,
    "description": "Payment for services",
    "request_id": "pix_123456789",
    "customer": {
      "customer_id": "12345678901",
      "metadata": {
        "name": "John Doe",
        "phone": "+5511999999999",
        "email": "john@example.com",
        "tax_id": "12345678901"
      }
    }
  }
  ```
</Request>

<Info>
  **Amount**: The `amount` field represents the fiat currency amount that will be charged, specified in the smallest unit (cents). For example, `2050` represents R$ 20.50 when currency is BRL, or $20.50 when currency is USD.
</Info>

<Info>
  **Currency**: The `currency` field specifies the conversion currency. Currently supported: `BRL` (Brazilian Real) and `USD` (US Dollar). We plan to expand support for more currencies in the future.
</Info>

<Info>
  **Request ID**: The `request_id` is a client-side identification ID that guarantees idempotency and will be sent via transaction webhook as `request_id`. This allows you to correlate webhook events with your original payment requests. Use a unique identifier for each payment request (e.g., UUID, timestamp-based ID, or your internal order ID). If you send the same `request_id` multiple times, the system will return the same transaction instead of creating duplicates.
</Info>

## Parameters

| Field | Type | Required | Validation | Description |
|-------|------|----------|------------|-------------|
| `amount` | integer | ✅ | `min=700` | Payment amount in smallest unit (cents for BRL/USD). Example: `2050` = R$ 20.50 or $20.50 |
| `currency` | string | ✅ | `"BRL"`, `"USD"` | Conversion currency. Currently supports BRL and USD, with more currencies planned for the future |
| `expires_in` | integer | ✅ | `min=120, max=1800` | Expiration time in seconds (minimum 120 seconds, maximum 1800 seconds / 30 minutes) |
| `description` | string | ❌ | `max=100` | Payment description |
| `request_id` | string | ✅ | `max=100` | Client-side identification ID that will be sent via transaction webhook as `request_id` |
| `customer` | object | ❌ | - | Customer information |

<Info>
  If `customer` is provided, all fields in `metadata` become required.
</Info>

## Status Codes

| Code | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `201` | Payment created successfully |
| `400` | Bad request - validation error |
| `401` | Unauthorized |
| `500` | Internal server error |

## Examples

### cURL

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.monkei.co/api/v1/transactions/payments/pix \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-API-Key: sk_live_1234567890abcdef" \
  -d '{
    "amount": 2050,
    "currency": "BRL",
    "expires_in": 1800,
    "description": "Payment for services",
    "request_id": "pix_123456789",
    "customer": {
      "customer_id": "12345678901",
      "metadata": {
        "name": "John Doe",
        "phone": "+5511999999999",
        "email": "john@example.com",
        "tax_id": "12345678901"
      }
    }
  }'
```

### JavaScript

```javascript
async function createPixPayment() {
  const response = await fetch('https://api.monkei.co/api/v1/transactions/payments/pix', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: {
      'Content-Type': 'application/json',
      'X-API-Key': 'sk_live_1234567890abcdef'
    },
    body: JSON.stringify({
      amount: 2050, // R$ 20,50 (in cents)
      currency: 'BRL',
      expires_in: 1800,
      description: 'Payment for services',
      request_id: `pix_${Date.now()}`,
      customer: {
        customer_id: '12345678901',
        metadata: {
          name: 'John Doe',
          phone: '+5511999999999',
          email: 'john@example.com',
          tax_id: '12345678901'
        }
      }
    })
  });

  const result = await response.json();
  if (result.success) {
    console.log('Transaction ID:', result.data.id);
    console.log('Fiat Amount (cents):', result.data.fiat_amount);
    console.log('QR Code (Base64):', result.data.qr_code);
    console.log('QR Code (Copy/Paste):', result.data.qr_code_url);
  }
  return result;
}
```

### Python

```python
import requests
import time

def create_pix_payment():
    headers = {
        'Content-Type': 'application/json',
        'X-API-Key': 'sk_live_1234567890abcdef'
    }
    
    data = {
        'amount': 2050,  # R$ 20.50 in cents
        'currency': 'BRL',
        'expires_in': 1800,
        'description': 'Payment for services',
        'request_id': f'pix_{int(time.time())}',
        'customer': {
            'customer_id': '12345678901',
            'metadata': {
                'name': 'John Doe',
                'phone': '+5511999999999',
                'email': 'john@example.com',
                'tax_id': '12345678901'
            }
        }
    }
    
    response = requests.post(
        'https://api.monkei.co/api/v1/transactions/payments/pix',
        headers=headers,
        json=data
    )
    
    result = response.json()
    if result.get('success'):
        print(f"Transaction ID: {result['data']['id']}")
        print(f"Fiat Amount (cents): {result['data']['fiat_amount']}")
    
    return result
```

## Response Fields

| Field | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| `success` | boolean | Indicates if the request was successful |
| `data` | object | Response data object |
| `data.id` | string | Transaction ID |
| `data.status` | string | Transaction status (PENDING, CONFIRMED, etc.) |
| `data.expires_in` | integer | Expiration time in seconds |
| `data.fiat_amount` | integer | Payment amount in fiat currency (smallest unit, e.g., cents for BRL/USD) |
| `data.qr_code` | string | Base64-encoded QR code image that can be directly embedded in HTML |
| `data.qr_code_url` | string | EMVCo standard QR code string that can be copied and pasted |
| `message` | string | Response message |

## QR Code Usage

The response includes two QR code formats:

1. **`qr_code`**: Base64-encoded image that can be directly embedded in HTML
2. **`qr_code_url`**: EMVCo standard QR code string that can be copied and pasted

### Displaying QR Code

```html
<img src="data:image/png;base64,{qr_code}" alt="PIX QR Code" />
```

## Payment Flow

<Steps>
  <Step title="Create Payment">
    Create a PIX payment using the API endpoint.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Display QR Code">
    Show the QR code to your customer (on screen or printed).
  </Step>
  <Step title="Customer Scans">
    Customer scans the QR code with their banking app.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Payment Confirmed">
    Payment is confirmed instantly and you receive a webhook notification.
  </Step>
</Steps>

## Important Notes

<Warning>
  The minimum payment amount is R$7.00. Amounts below this will be rejected.
</Warning>

<Info>
  The `amount` field represents the fiat currency amount that will be charged, specified in the smallest unit. For PIX payments, this is always in BRL (cents). The `fiat_amount` field in the response shows the original amount in cents.
</Info>

<Info>
  The `currency` field specifies the conversion currency. Currently, we support `BRL` (Brazilian Real) and `USD` (US Dollar). We plan to expand support for more currencies in the future.
</Info>

<Info>
  The `request_id` is a client-side identification ID that guarantees idempotency and will be sent via transaction webhook as `request_id`. This allows you to correlate webhook events with your original payment requests. Make sure to use a unique identifier for each payment request. If you send the same `request_id` multiple times, the system will return the same transaction instead of creating duplicates.
</Info>

<Info>
  PIX payments are processed instantly. Once the customer scans and confirms, the payment is settled immediately.
</Info>

## Error Handling

### Common Errors

| Code | Description | Solution |
|------|-------------|----------|
| `VALIDATION_ERROR` | Invalid field value | Check field 'amount' must be at least 700 (R$ 7.00 or $7.00) |
| `INVALID_EXPIRATION` | Expiration too short | Set at least 120 seconds |
